subject: Manifest: POC success metrics, owners, and next steps (Carmine AI)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Mira Cho <mira@carmine.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Manifest: POC success metrics, owners, and next steps (Carmine AI)

Hi Mira / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, here is a concise POC manifest we discussed so your engineering and product teams can validate the scope quickly. Objective: validate that Redwood Inference can meet performance and quality targets for Carmine’s multi-turn summarization pipeline under a representative workload.

High-level trial plan (2 weeks):
- Kickoff & integration window: days 0–3 (API keys, test dataset ingestion, network checks).
- Baseline runs and smoke tests: days 4–6.
- Targeted evaluation and regression checks: days 7–12.
- Readout and next steps: day 13–14.

Success criteria (pass/fail gates):
1) Latency: P95 response time <= 250 ms for 1k-token average requests in the test harness (95th percentile measured across 1,000 requests).
2) Throughput: sustained 120 requests/sec at 99% availability for 5-minute windows during peak traffic simulations.
3) Token cost: average per-token cost <= $0.005 (model+runtime) for the chosen quantized runtime profile (note: dashboard will show token breakdown).
4) Quality: automated eval on the labeled validation set — mean ROUGE-L >= 0.68 and human-sampled satisfaction >= 90% (we will run a 50-sample blind review).
5) Stability: no more than 1 retries per 1,000 requests and error rate <= 0.5%.

Owners (who will drive each item):
- Integration + runbook: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.ai) — infra hooks, test harness, logging.
- Latency/throughput experiments & kernel profile tuning: Grace O'Connor (grace@redwood.ai).
- Cost measurement & billing estimates: Olga Petrov (olga@redwood.ai) + Finance (if needed).
- Quality evals (label set + blind review): Carmine (Mira/Tom) provide initial labeled subset; Redwood will run automated metrics and coordinate blind review.

Deliverables we will produce:
- Shared POC workbook (attached: carmine_poc_workbook.xlsx) with test cases, example payloads, and measurement templates.
- Short runbook for onboarding (network requirements, sample cURL calls).
- 2 summary dashboards: perf (latency/throughput) and cost breakdown by model step.

Action items / next steps (please reply with owners / availability):
1) Carmine: provide sample labeled validation set (minimum 250 items) and an initial forecast of expected concurrency (baseline and burst) — owner: Mira / Tom.
2) Redwood: provision trial model endpoint and share API keys (Ben) — ETA: 48 hours after dataset is shared.
3) Network check: confirm egress rules and IP allowlist (attachment: network_diagram.png) — owner: Carmine infra.
4) Confirm final model variant for the trial (we recommended Redwood-moderate-quant) — decision from Carmine by EOD Wednesday.

Attachments: carmine_poc_workbook.xlsx (workbook template), network_diagram.png (suggested allowlist topology).

If this manifest looks good, reply with dataset link and preferred kickoff time tomorrow or Wednesday. Happy to tighten any metric if you want a more conservative gate.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Solutions Eng, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0168

---
From: Mira Cho <mira@carmine.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom@carmine.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Manifest: POC success metrics, owners, and next steps (Carmine AI)

Thanks, Olga — this is very clear and helpful. Quick clarifications from our side before we finalize: 

1) Throughput: 120 req/s sustained sounds reasonable, but our realistic burst is closer to 200 req/s during peak business hours. Can Redwood show behaviour up to 200 req/s in a single stress run, and then we measure the sustained 120 req/s gate separately? We don’t need the 200 req/s as an acceptance gate, just visibility.

2) Cost: $0.005/token is acceptable as a target for the POC but we need a breakdown by model variant (we may evaluate a slightly larger variant if quality gains justify the cost).

3) Dataset: I’ll share a Google Drive link (private) with 400 labeled samples by EOD today — will include a column with the business-critical fields you should evaluate.

4) Allowlist: we need a short-window IP for the initial sandbox (Tom will coordinate).

Preferred kickoff: Wednesday 21 Oct, 09:30 PT — are you able to start the integration then?

Thanks, Mira
Director, Product — Carmine AI
mira@carmine.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Mira Cho <mira@carmine.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Manifest: POC success metrics, owners, and next steps (Carmine AI)

Hi Mira — great, Wednesday 09:30 PT works. A few operational notes so the kickoff is productive: 

- When you share the Drive link please include a service-account-accessible ACL (or we can accept an S3 presigned URL). Ben will need read access to ingest the labeled set.
- We will run two stress profiles during the POC window:
  * Profile A: 120 req/s sustained for 30 minutes (measures steady-state tail latency).
  * Profile B: 200 req/s 60-second spike (measures degradation modes and fallback behavior).
- For the 200 req/s spike we will capture per-interval (10s) metrics so you can see the slope of latency and error rates. No gating on Profile B — informational only.
- On the model variant question: we will run both Redwood-moderate-quant (default) and Redwood-large-quant in parallel for a subset of the test set to show quality vs cost tradeoffs. Expect separate cost curves in the final report.

Operational owner table (quick):
- Ben: endpoint provisioning, test harness, ingestion.
- Grace: perf tuning and kernel selection; will own the perf dashboard.
- Olga: POC oversight, success decision, and billing estimates.

Ben
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — confirming final plan and updated gates below after Ben’s notes and Mira’s ask.

Final trial dates: kickoff Wed 2026-10-21 09:30 PT — run window 21–34 Oct (two-week window, readout on Fri 2026-10-23).

Updated success gates:
- Latency: P95 <= 250 ms (primary gate).
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s (gate); 200 req/s spike (informational only).
- Cost: target <= $0.005/token for Redwood-moderate-quant; comparison curve for Redwood-large-quant.
- Quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.68 automated AND 90% human satisfaction on the blind 50-sample set.
- Stability: error rate <= 0.5% over the run window.

Deliverables at readout (Fri 2026-10-23):
- Perf dashboard link + CSV export (latency, throughput, errors).
- Cost breakdown CSV by model variant and by test-case.
- Short runbook with steps to promote to Dedicated if you choose to continue.

Outstanding items for Carmine (please confirm by EOD Monday):
1) Drive link with 400 labeled samples + service account ACL (Mira).
2) IP allowlist or temporary VPN window (Tom).
3) Final model variant preference (if you want to bias the trial toward large-quant).

We’ll attach the final workbook to the readout email and share the dashboard. Looking forward to the kickoff — Ben will send the sandbox endpoint and keys once we have dataset access.

Best,
Olga
